werk/muhal-richard-abrams-1-oqa-19.text:
Muhal Richard Abrams recorded this album in November and December 1977 at Generation Sound Studios in New York. It was released on the Italian label Black Saint. Abrams plays piano, synthesizer and voice, and surrounds himself with a quintet of Anthony Braxton, Henry Threadgill, Leonard Jones and Steve McCall.

According to AllMusic, this group made demanding music, harmonically dense and rhythmically unpredictable. Braxton's fast solos are answered by Threadgill's more bluesy lines, while Abrams holds jazz, blues and other sources together. The Penguin Guide called the music intricate and seldom immediately appealing, and the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide felt that Abrams had never sounded better as the leader of a small group.
werk/muhal-richard-abrams-1-oqa-19.listen: Listen to Charlie In the Parker and notice how piano, horns and rhythm section weave in and out of one another.

werk/muhal-richard-abrams-afrisong.text:
Afrisong is a solo piano album by Muhal Richard Abrams. He recorded the seven pieces on 9 September 1975 at Universal Recording Studios in Chicago. The album was released on India Navigation and on the Japanese label Trio/Whynot. All the compositions are his own.

AllMusic writes that stride, bebop, blues and free music flow effortlessly into one another here. The record also shows off his technical skill and his underrated piano playing, which often disappears into the background behind his work as an arranger, composer and bandleader. The Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide calls the album the best of his early solo work. It lasts about forty minutes, with The New People as the longest piece at just over ten minutes.
werk/muhal-richard-abrams-afrisong.listen: Listen to Blues For M. and notice which bluesy elements you can hear in the piano playing.

werk/muhal-richard-abrams-sightsong.text:
Sightsong was released in 1976 on the Italian label Black Saint. It is a duo record by pianist Muhal Richard Abrams and bassist Malachi Favors, who also played with the Art Ensemble of Chicago. The whole recording thus consists of nothing but piano and bass.

The pieces last roughly five to six minutes. Two of them are dedicated to jazz musicians, Wilbur Ware and Johnny Griffin, and a third to the AACM. AllMusic called it one of Abrams's best recordings and the best opportunity to hear Favors outside his work with the Art Ensemble. The Penguin Guide spoke of an example of the radical yet traditional spirit that Abrams had done so much to promote.
werk/muhal-richard-abrams-sightsong.listen: Listen to Sightsong and notice how piano and bass talk to each other, with neither of them simply accompanying.

werk/muhal-richard-abrams-things-to-come.text:
Things to Come from Those Now Gone is Muhal Richard Abrams's third album, released in 1975 on Delmark. He plays piano and performs seven of his own compositions with changing line-ups: Wallace McMillan, Edwin Daugherty, Richard Brown, Emanuel Cranshaw, Reggie Willis, Rufus Reid, Steve McCall and Wilbur Campbell. On one track Ella Jackson sings.

Critics heard a very varied whole. AllMusic speaks of a mixed bag with work ranging from strangely bad to stunningly beautiful. The Penguin Guide to Jazz sees in the record a powerful affirmation of the conviction that musical progress comes only by following the lessons of tradition. According to the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide, the album shows the AACM in the middle of the decade, with chamber ballads, hard bop, electronics, a mock opera and plenty of energy.
werk/muhal-richard-abrams-things-to-come.listen: Listen to How Are You? and notice Ella Jackson's singing between the piano, vibraphone and bass.

werk/mulatu-astatke-sketches-of-ethiopia.text:
Sketches of Ethiopia was released in August 2013 on Jazz Village. Mulatu Astatke is accompanied by the Steps Ahead Band, which has nothing to do with the fusion group Steps Ahead. As on his previous album, Mulatu Steps Ahead, Ethiopian instruments such as the washint, the krar and the masinko can be heard.

The opening track is an arrangement of Azmari, written by Russ Gershon. The album closes with Surma, a collaboration with the Malian singer Fatoumata Diawara, who co-wrote the song with him. The Quietus heard urban club tempos alongside traditional rural folk, with Latin percussion and Afrofunk rhythms. According to The Independent, the founder of Ethio-jazz thus remains the undisputed master.
werk/mulatu-astatke-sketches-of-ethiopia.listen: Listen to Surma with Fatoumata Diawara and notice how her voice relates to the instruments.

werk/mumford-en-sons-babel.text:
With Babel, Mumford & Sons released the follow-up to Sigh No More, which had made them internationally famous in 2009, on 21 September 2012. Markus Dravs produced again, and the album was released on Island Records. The band had been playing new songs live since late 2010, including Broken Crown and Below My Feet. They decided not to change their sound, but did take the time to refine it. Not With Haste is a rewritten version of Learn Me Right, which they recorded with Birdy for the film Brave. I Will Wait was the first single.

The reviews were mostly positive. Mojo thought it was more than a solid nu-folk album and also called it a good pop album. Babel went straight to number one in both Britain and the United States and was the fastest-selling album of the British year in 2012. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year.
werk/mumford-en-sons-babel.listen: Listen to I Will Wait and notice how little the band has changed its sound since Sigh No More, and where you still hear something new.

werk/mumford-en-sons-little-lion-man.text: In the summer of 2009, Little Lion Man by Mumford & Sons from London was released, taken from the album Sigh No More. There is a banjo and an acoustic guitar, but the kick drum and the build-up come from stadium rock: folk rock on an arena scale. The album sold millions of copies. In the decade that followed, hip hop, pop and dance almost entirely took over the charts, and things went quiet for rock.
werk/mumford-en-sons-little-lion-man.listen: In The Cave, hear the banjo picking quickly above the acoustic guitar, and how the kick drum pushes the song towards a big chorus.

werk/mumford-en-sons-sigh-no-more.text:
As the debut album of the British folk rock band Mumford & Sons, Sigh No More was released in the United Kingdom on 2 October 2009. In the United States and Canada the record followed only in February 2010. Markus Dravs produced. The four band members swap between banjo, double bass, mandolin, accordion, organ and drums, and guest musicians joined for strings and brass. Little Lion Man was the first single, followed by Winter Winds, The Cave and Roll Away Your Stone.

The album was a slow burner. It entered at number 11 in the British chart and reached number two only after more than a year, after it won the Brit Award for British Album of the Year in February 2011. It had earlier been nominated for the Mercury Prize. Critics responded generally positively. In the United States it also reached number two on the Billboard 200 in early 2011.
werk/mumford-en-sons-sigh-no-more.listen: Listen to Little Lion Man and notice how the acoustic instruments and the group harmonies drive the song forward.

werk/mumford-en-sons-wilder-mind.text:
At the end of 2013, the members of Mumford & Sons were thinking of a long break, but after five months they were back at work. They wrote and recorded demos in the garage of Aaron Dessner of The National in Brooklyn and at Eastcote Studios in London. They recorded the album itself at AIR Studios with producer James Ford, who also occasionally sat behind the drums.

After two albums with Markus Dravs, the band left behind its characteristic acoustic instruments, such as the banjo and the double bass. Electric guitars and a session drummer took their place. Critics heard indie rock and electric, guitar-driven stadium rock. In 2015 the album went straight to number one in its first week in the United Kingdom and the United States.
werk/mumford-en-sons-wilder-mind.listen: Listen to Believe and notice which instruments you hear: what is left of the banjo and the double bass of the earlier albums?

werk/muse-absolution.text:
For their third album the band took their time, because earlier recordings had been rushed. In early 2002 they rented a country house near Brighton to write, and during that period their American label dropped them. Most of the work took place at Grouse Lodge in Ireland, under heavy pressure from quarrels with the record company and a lawsuit. Singer Matt Bellamy later spoke of a sense of impending doom. Producer Rich Costey wanted a bigger, more aggressive sound. He kept editing to a minimum for a human sound, and used the Kyma system for much of the sound processing. For the intro of Apocalypse Please, the band recorded two bass drums in the studio's swimming pool.

The album mixes rock with orchestra, as in Butterflies and Hurricanes and Blackout, and has apocalyptic themes. Stockholm Syndrome, Time Is Running Out, Hysteria and Sing for Absolution were released as singles. Time Is Running Out became the group's first top ten single in England.
werk/muse-absolution.listen: Listen to Apocalypse Please and notice the space and power of the drums at the start.

werk/muse-black-holes-and-revelations.text:
After Absolution, the band withdrew to Studio Miraval, an old castle in the south of France, to write without a deadline. Producer Rich Costey joined them two weeks later. Progress was slow, and the group moved to New York, where Matt Bellamy visited the clubs and learned to DJ. You can hear that in the dance rhythms of Supermassive Black Hole and Map of the Problematique. The band bought old synthesizers, such as a Buchla 200e, and learned to work with them. Most of the work took place in New York, with the finishing touches in Italy. The album took about four months.

The influences range from Depeche Mode to Sly and the Family Stone and music from southern Italy. Knights of Cydonia has a mariachi trumpet and a galloping drum rhythm, and ends with a guitar solo. The lyrics deal with political corruption, alien invasion and revolution, alongside ordinary love songs. The album received good reviews and appeared on year-end lists.
werk/muse-black-holes-and-revelations.listen: Listen to Knights of Cydonia and notice the mariachi trumpet and the galloping drum rhythm.

werk/muse-origin-of-symmetry.text:
Origin of Symmetry is the second studio album by the English band Muse and was released on 18 June 2001. The producers are John Leckie and David Bottrill. After the tour for the debut Showbiz, the group first recorded four songs with Bottrill, including Plug In Baby, Bliss and New Born. Leckie followed, with recordings at places including Sawmills in Cornwall, Real World Studios and David Gilmour's houseboat Astoria. For Megalomania the band recorded a church organ in a church in Bath.

Matt Bellamy now wrote about science fiction instead of broken hearts. The album is regarded as their breakthrough, reached number three in the United Kingdom and received mostly good reviews for its mix of rock and classical. It was not released in the United States until 2005.
werk/muse-origin-of-symmetry.listen: Listen to Plug In Baby, one of the songs from the first recording session with Bottrill, and notice the guitar.

werk/muse-plug-in-baby.text: In March 2001, Plug In Baby by Muse was released, a band from the small English seaside town of Teignmouth. Singer and guitarist Matt Bellamy played fast runs that sounded like classical music, with lots of effects. Muse carried on the line of progressive rock and Queen: big, dramatic and technical. In the years that followed they became one of the biggest stadium bands in Europe.
werk/muse-plug-in-baby.listen: The guitar riff of Plug In Baby sounds like a fast run by Bach, but played through a distorted guitar.

werk/muse-showbiz.text:
Showbiz is the debut album of the English rock band Muse. It was released in France on 7 September 1999 on Naïve Records and in the United Kingdom on 4 October on Taste Media. The recording took place in April and May 1999 at RAK Studios and Sawmills Studio. John Leckie, who also produced Radiohead's The Bends, worked with the band and Paul Reeve on the production.

From some fifty songs by Matt Bellamy, the group chose the most straightforward pieces. More experimental songs were released as B-sides. The sound is alternative rock with subtle influences of classical, jazz, blues and Latin American music. Uno, Cave, Muscle Museum, Sunburn and Unintended were released as singles. Many critics compared the band to Radiohead. The album reached number 29 in the British album chart.
werk/muse-showbiz.listen: Listen to Unintended and notice Matt Bellamy's singing.

werk/muse-the-resistance.text:
The Resistance, Muse's fifth studio album, was released on 14 September 2009. The band produced it themselves in their own studio in Como, Italy, between September 2008 and May 2009. For the lyrics, Bellamy drew inspiration from George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four. As a result the record revolves around politics and oppression, and the music mixes rock with orchestra and electronics.

Uprising became the first single. According to Bellamy, Undisclosed Desires is the first Muse song without guitar or piano, with an influence of R&B and synth bass. The closer is Exogenesis, a symphony in three parts lasting thirteen minutes, with an orchestra of more than forty musicians, about the end of humanity. Critics praised the concept and the vocals, but some found it over the top and a copy of Queen. In 2011 the record won a Grammy for Best Rock Album.
werk/muse-the-resistance.listen: Listen to Undisclosed Desires and notice that you hear no guitar and no piano. Follow the synth bass and the rhythm instead.

werk/my-bloody-valentine-isn-t-anything.text:
Isn't Anything is the debut album of My Bloody Valentine and was released on 21 November 1988 on Creation Records. After singer Dave Conway left and Bilinda Butcher took his place, Kevin Shields went back to the group's experimental roots. He explored the possibilities of the studio, first on the single You Made Me Realise. Label boss Alan McGee urged the band to concentrate on the stranger work, such as Soft as Snow. Most of it was recorded in two weeks in a studio in Wales, during which the members slept about two hours a night.

The sound has soft vocals and ingratiating melodies, heard as if through a curtain of hazy, distorted guitar noise. The result was an important example of shoegaze. Critics responded enthusiastically, and the record topped the British independent chart. One reviewer called the album the first full expression of this new sound.
werk/my-bloody-valentine-isn-t-anything.listen: Listen to Soft as Snow (But Warm Inside) and notice how the soft vocals half disappear behind hazy guitars.

werk/my-bloody-valentine-loveless.text:
Loveless took My Bloody Valentine almost three years. The recording ran from February 1989 to September 1991 and took place in nineteen different studios. Kevin Shields led the sessions and experimented with glide guitar, unusual tunings, sampling and meticulous studio technique. Creation Records had thought that the album would be finished in five days. The press spoke of costs of £250,000, a figure that Shields disputes.

The music is called shoegaze, noise pop and dream pop. Most of it was written and played by Shields. With the tremolo arm he bent the strings slightly out of tune, so that the guitars sound like many layers, while according to him there are fewer guitar tracks than on most demos. The album reached number 24 in the British chart and was praised, but Creation dropped the band afterwards. It is regarded as a milestone of shoegaze and influenced many later artists.
werk/my-bloody-valentine-loveless.listen: Listen to i only said and notice the guitar, which sounds as if a wah-wah pedal is being used, although Shields created that effect with an equaliser during recording.

werk/my-bloody-valentine-m-b-v.text:
My Bloody Valentine released m b v themselves on 2 February 2013, more than twenty years after Loveless. Kevin Shields produced it. The recording began in 1996 and was half finished when the band split up in 1997. In 2006, after the reunion, Shields picked it up again and combined the old material with new recordings. The final vocals, bass and drums followed in 2011 and 2012. She Found Now was the only track recorded entirely from scratch, in 2012. The album was recorded and mixed on analogue equipment, on tape and without digital editing.

The sound is shoegaze and noise pop. Shields wanted less to build another world as on Loveless and more to sound like Isn't Anything, rawer and sprawling. The Beach Boys and their unfinished album Smile were an influence: he deliberately did not write in terms of beginning, middle and end. The album received rave reviews and appeared on many lists for 2013.
werk/my-bloody-valentine-m-b-v.listen: Listen to She Found Now and notice how the guitars and the vocals flow into one another.

werk/n-w-a-straight-outta-compton.text:
Straight Outta Compton is the debut album of N.W.A and was released in January 1989 on Priority and Ruthless Records. Dr. Dre, DJ Yella and Arabian Prince produced, and the lyrics came from Eazy-E, Ice Cube and MC Ren, with help from The D.O.C. Ruthless was founded in 1987 by Eric Wright, who also rapped as Eazy-E. Until then, hip hop in Los Angeles had been mostly dance-oriented. This album described life in Compton, with hostility towards rivals and police.

Fuck tha Police earned the group a warning letter from an FBI official, and MTV refused the video for the title track. Despite little radio airplay outside Los Angeles, it became the first gangsta rap album to go platinum, in July 1989. The first reviews were mixed, but later the record was regarded as one of the most influential in hip hop history. In 2016 the album entered the Grammy Hall of Fame, as the first rap album.
werk/n-w-a-straight-outta-compton.listen: In Straight Outta Compton, listen to how the voices of the three rappers alternate above the hard, bare beat.

werk/nat-king-cole-love-is-the-thing.text:
In 1956, Cole teamed up with arranger Gordon Jenkins to make the first of four albums that critics count among the best of both musicians. The album was released in 1957 on Capitol Records, with Lee Gillette as producer and Charlie LaVere on piano.

Cole sticks entirely to the role he had been given in the 1950s, that of an outstanding ballad singer. His restrained way of singing suits Jenkins's quiet string arrangements. You can hardly hear the singer's jazz roots in it; it is above all a romantic album. Stardust was released as a single. The album reached number 1 on the Billboard chart and was Cole's first gold album. It remained beloved for years afterwards.
werk/nat-king-cole-love-is-the-thing.listen: Listen to Stardust and notice how calmly the strings carry the tempo, so that Cole's soft voice has all the space it needs.

werk/nat-king-cole-sings-for-two-in-love.text:
This 1953 album contains standards in arrangements by Nelson Riddle. It was first released as a 10-inch LP with eight tracks and was expanded with four songs in 1955 for the larger 12-inch format. Nat King Cole sings, Riddle arranges and conducts.

The songs come from the American songbook tradition, from Gershwin and Rodgers and Hart to Lerner and Loewe. Love Is Here to Stay, This Can't Be Love, Tenderly and There Will Never Be Another You, among others, are on the record. The title is sometimes shortened to Sings for Two in Love or simply Two in Love. The album reached number 8 on the Billboard chart of best-selling pop albums.
werk/nat-king-cole-sings-for-two-in-love.listen: In Love Is Here to Stay, listen to how voice and orchestra take turns with the melody.

werk/nat-king-cole-unforgettable.text:
This album is a collection of recordings that Nat King Cole made for Capitol in the early 1950s. It was released in 1952 as a 10-inch LP and reissued in 1954 as a 12-inch LP, with four extra tracks. The producer was Lee Gillette.

The record shows Cole's singing in varying settings. On Unforgettable, Pretend, Answer Me, My Love and Make Her Mine the orchestra of Nelson Riddle plays, on Mona Lisa and Too Young that of Les Baxter. A few songs were recorded with the Nat King Cole Trio, such as What'll I Do? and Lost April, and on Lost April and A Portrait of Jennie the Carlyle Hall Strings play. Trio, strings and big orchestra thus stand side by side on one and the same record. The opening track gave the collection its title.
werk/nat-king-cole-unforgettable.listen: In Unforgettable, listen to how the orchestra of Nelson Riddle accompanies Cole's voice.

werk/ne-yo-because-of-you.text:
After the success of his debut, Ne-Yo went back into the studio in 2007, with many of the same collaborators: Ron Neff-U Feemster, Stargate and Shea Taylor. New names joined them, such as The Heavyweights, Eric Hudson and Knobody. Plans to work with Timbaland fell through because of schedules. The working title was Know Me, but a month before release the album was named after the first single: the singer wanted to express his thanks to the people who inspire him.

The guests are Jay-Z on Crazy and Jennifer Hudson on Leaving Tonight. The songs are mostly about love and longing, sometimes soft and restrained, sometimes with more tempo. Reviewers thought the album a step forward from the debut. It topped the American album chart and won the 2008 Grammy Award for Best Contemporary R&B Album.
werk/ne-yo-because-of-you.listen: Listen to Because of You and notice the upbeat tempo and the singing about the people who inspire the singer. Hear how this song has more momentum than the calm love songs further on in the album.

werk/ne-yo-in-my-own-words.text:
Before he sang himself, Ne-Yo wrote songs for others. His breakthrough came in 2004 with Let Me Love You, a worldwide hit for Mario. He then signed with Def Jam and made his debut album, which was released in February 2006. He worked with Ron Neff-U Feemster, Shea Taylor and the Norwegian production duo Stargate, among others, and wrote the lyrics of all the songs himself.

The sound is smooth, understated R&B with a nod here and there to the soul of the 1970s and 1980s. Stay introduced the singer to the public, but So Sick, a quiet song by Stargate, became the big hit. Critics were mostly positive and noted how focused the album was for a debut with so many producers. It received a Grammy nomination and entered at number one in the United States.
werk/ne-yo-in-my-own-words.listen: Listen to So Sick and notice how calm the rhythm stays while the vocals are about a broken relationship. Observe how little the production needs to carry that feeling.

werk/ne-yo-libra-scale.text:
Libra Scale was released in Japan first, in October 2010, then in the United Kingdom, and on 22 November in the United States, as Ne-Yo's fourth album. It is a concept album. He drew inspiration from science fiction, comics and Japanese animation, and from Michael Jackson, especially Thriller, Moonwalker and Bad. At first he thought of a short film, but because of time and money it became six extended music videos. The story is about three garbage men, including Jerome, who gain power and fame on condition that they never fall in love. The title refers to his star sign.

The singles were Beautiful Monster, Champagne Life and One in a Million. Rolling Stone called it in effect a tribute album to Michael Jackson. Other critics found the story a little silly but thought the electronic tracks the strongest.
werk/ne-yo-libra-scale.listen: Listen to Beautiful Monster, the Europop single from the album, and notice the danceable, electronic production.

werk/ne-yo-year-of-the-gentleman.text:
Year of the Gentleman was released on 16 September 2008 on Compound Entertainment and Def Jam, as Ne-Yo's third album. As on the two earlier records, he worked with Stargate, Reggie Syience Perry and Shea Taylor, but he also found new collaborators, such as Chuck Harmony and Polow da Don. The title refers to the Rat Pack of the 1960s, with Frank Sinatra and Sammy Davis Jr.: their polished style was meant to resonate in his music as well. There are no guest vocalists.

The singles Closer and Miss Independent became international hits, followed by Mad and Part of the List. The record earned six Grammy nominations, including Album of the Year. Rolling Stone called it a concept album about what a great friend he can be. Others found it uneven and too ballad-heavy.
werk/ne-yo-year-of-the-gentleman.listen: Listen to Closer, the first single, and notice how the vocals try to strike the polished, elegant tone of the album title.

werk/neil-sedaka-emergence.text:
Emergence was released in September 1971 on RCA Victor, the label that had dropped Neil Sedaka at the end of 1966. It was therefore a short reunion. In some countries the album appeared on Kirshner Records, Don Kirshner's own label. He wrote all the songs together with Howard Greenfield.

The album was not a success in the shops, but it has acquired cult status among fans. Four songs were also released as singles: I'm a Song (Sing Me) with Silent Movies, and Superbird with Rosemary Blue. The album opens with I'm a Song (Sing Me) and closes with a reprise of that song. Of all the records Sedaka made, Emergence is his own favourite.
werk/neil-sedaka-emergence.listen: Listen to I'm a Song (Sing Me) and compare it with the reprise at the end of the album. What has changed in the way the song sounds?

werk/neil-young-after-the-gold-rush.text:
Young lived in Topanga Canyon, an artists' community in Southern California, and recorded the album largely in his own studio at home. For months he struggled with writer's block, until the actor Dean Stockwell let him read a screenplay with the same title. It was about an ecological disaster that washes away the hippie community. According to Stockwell, Young then wrote the songs in three weeks. The film never materialised, and only After the Gold Rush and Cripple Creek Ferry really have anything to do with it. Players from Crazy Horse and from Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young took part, and Nils Lofgren was heard for the first time.

The album consists mostly of country folk, with a few rock songs such as Southern Man. The first reactions were mixed. Later it earned a place on many lists of the best albums of all time. In 2014 it went into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/neil-young-after-the-gold-rush.listen: Listen to After the Gold Rush and notice the lyrics, which are based on a dream about a future in which humanity flees into space after the environmental disaster.

werk/neil-young-american-stars-n-bars.text:
This 1977 album was assembled from recordings spread over 29 months. After Zuma and a tour with Crazy Horse, Neil Young worked with Stephen Stills again. In April 1977 he recorded a number of country rock songs for the first side. For the second side he drew on older material from sessions of 1974 to 1976. Homegrown and Star of Bethlehem were intended for an album that was shelved. On Star of Bethlehem, Emmylou Harris sings along.

The best-known song is Like a Hurricane, about a stormy love affair, which he wrote on an electric organ and a string synthesizer. Bite the Bullet combines outlaw country with punk, and Homegrown is a light-hearted ode to marijuana. The album reached number 21 on the Billboard 200 and was certified gold.
werk/neil-young-american-stars-n-bars.listen: Listen to Like a Hurricane and notice how the song gives musical shape to the stormy love of the lyrics.

werk/neil-young-comes-a-time.text:
After the success of Harvest in 1972, Neil Young did not want to remain the image of the sensitive singer-songwriter, and for years he made records in widely differing styles. With Comes a Time he returned to a romantic folk style. The first sessions took place in September 1977 in Florida, where he recorded almost everything alone with acoustic guitars. When Reprise boss Mo Ostin asked for rhythm tracks, sessions followed in November in Nashville with a full band, including musicians from Harvest.

Nicolette Larson sings along on most of the songs. On five tracks more than thirty musicians play, which gives a country wall of sound. Lotta Love and Look Out for My Love date from 1976, with Crazy Horse. Many songs are about relationships, such as Already One, about Carrie Snodgress and their son. He himself calls it one of his best albums. Four Strong Winds closes the album, a cover of the Canadian folk song by Ian and Sylvia.
werk/neil-young-comes-a-time.listen: In Comes a Time, listen to how Nicolette Larson's voice wraps itself around the lead vocal. Notice the large group of acoustic guitars underneath.

werk/neil-young-harvest.text:
After After the Gold Rush and the tour with Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, Neil Young withdrew to his new ranch in California at the end of 1970. There he injured his back, which meant he could no longer stand during performances and played mainly acoustically. An appearance on The Johnny Cash Show led to a collaboration with producer Elliot Mazer and Nashville session musicians, whom he called the Stray Gators. He recorded most of the album wearing a back brace.

On two songs the London Symphony Orchestra plays, and guests such as David Crosby, Graham Nash, Linda Ronstadt, Stephen Stills and James Taylor sing along. Old Man is about the ranch's caretaker. Heart of Gold became his only number one in the United States. It was the best-selling album in America in 1972. The success overwhelmed the singer, who would rather have stepped out of the spotlight.
werk/neil-young-harvest.listen: In Old Man, listen to the lyrics: they are about the old man who came with the ranch when he bought it.

werk/neil-young-neil-young.text:
After the break-up of Buffalo Springfield, Neil Young made his first solo record in 1968. His manager Elliot Roberts arranged a contract with Reprise, and David Briggs became his producer for the first time. Briggs would produce almost all of his albums. The songs were recorded between August and October 1968 in various studios in Los Angeles, largely by laying down the instruments one by one. He later turned away from that approach.

The songs come from different times. The Old Laughing Lady was written three years earlier, on napkins in a coffee house. The Loner is a guitar-driven rock song that points ahead to his next album. The Emperor of Wyoming and String Quartet from Whiskey Boot Hill are instrumentals. The record was released in November 1968 and did not make the Billboard 200.
werk/neil-young-neil-young.listen: Listen to The Loner and notice how the guitar carries this rock song.

werk/neil-young-on-the-beach.text:
After the enormous success of Harvest, Neil Young deliberately chose what he called the ditch: a rougher road with more interesting people. On the Beach is the second part of his Ditch Trilogy and was recorded after Tonight's the Night but released earlier. The July 1974 album expressed feelings of overexposure, alienation and wistfulness. The recording was sloppy, with session musicians swapping instruments, and Young opted for raw mixes.

It is a folk rock record about anger, alienation and cautious optimism. Walk On opens with the wish to carry on. Revolution Blues was inspired by Charles Manson, whom Young had met shortly before. Motion Pictures is a farewell to his relationship with the actress Carrie Snodgress, and Ambulance Blues closes the album. Sales were disappointing and Rolling Stone called it one of the most despairing albums of the decade. Later it was held in high regard.
werk/neil-young-on-the-beach.listen: In Walk On, listen to how wistfulness and the wish to carry on alternate within a single song.

werk/neil-young-ragged-glory.text:
Ragged Glory is Neil Young's twentieth studio album and his sixth with the band Crazy Horse. It was released in September 1990 on Reprise. The recording took place in April 1990 at Young's Broken Arrow Ranch. For two weeks the band played a set of songs twice a day, then listened back and chose the best takes. According to Young, that took the analysis out of the sessions and the group did not have to think.

The record returns to the heavy rock of Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere and Zuma, with long guitar jams: two songs last longer than ten minutes. Country Home and White Line date from the mid-1970s. Farmer John is a cover that came about spontaneously during the work. A Rolling Stone reviewer called the album a monument to the spirit of the garage, to passion over precision. Christgau spoke of an atavistic garage stomp.
werk/neil-young-ragged-glory.listen: In Love to Burn, listen to the band's guitars and notice how loosely and spontaneously they play together.

werk/neil-young-southern-man.text: On 19 September 1970, After the Gold Rush by the Canadian singer Neil Young was released. On the song Southern Man he denounced the racism and slavery in the southern United States. With Alabama he did so again two years later. Young played both soft folk and hard guitar rock, and later became a model for grunge bands. His songs provoked a well-known answer from the South.
werk/neil-young-southern-man.listen: In Southern Man you hear Young's sharp, distorted electric guitar above the piano. The lyrics are an indictment.

werk/neil-young-tonight-s-the-night.text:
This record is a direct expression of grief. In the months before the songs came about, Danny Whitten, guitarist of Crazy Horse, and Neil Young's friend and roadie Bruce Berry had both died of an overdose. The recording took place in August and September 1973, mostly on 26 August. The band was called the Santa Monica Flyers: Young, Ben Keith, Nils Lofgren and the rhythm section of Crazy Horse. It was the first time the surviving members of Crazy Horse had played together since Whitten's death.

The title song mentions Berry by name. Come On Baby Let's Go Downtown comes from a 1970 concert and features Whitten's guitar and vocal work. The album was not released until June 1975 and is the third record of the so-called Ditch Trilogy, which followed the success of Harvest.
werk/neil-young-tonight-s-the-night.listen: Listen to Tonight's the Night and notice the lyrics, which speak of Bruce Berry's death without beating around the bush.

werk/nelson-riddle-the-tender-touch.text:
The Tender Touch is Nelson Riddle's second studio album, released in 1956. It followed the first album by his orchestra from the year before, a collection of pop arrangements of tunes from the musical Oklahoma! The sleeve note promises the most romantic love songs, melodies as soft as a caress. Capitol Records released the album in December 1956, at the same time as the compilation This Is Sinatra! It was a busy year for the arranger: he wrote the music for the film Johnny Concho, worked on Nat King Cole's last instrumental album and had topped the charts for four weeks with Lisbon Antigua.

Within a month, Billboard counted The Tender Touch among the ten best instrumental pop records. The British World Record Club later issued it under the title Relax with Nelson Riddle.
werk/nelson-riddle-the-tender-touch.listen: In Love Letters, listen to how the orchestra makes the melody sound like a romantic song.

werk/nena-feuer-und-flamme.text:
Feuer und Flamme was released in 1985 and is the third album of the German pop group, and the fourth studio album of the singer Gabriele Kerner, who became known as Nena. It followed the success of 99 Luftballons from 1984. The album was successful and reached number two in Germany.

After that success, Nena made an English-language version of the album, It's All in the Game, with lyrics by the Canadian singer Lisa Dalbello. That experiment failed commercially and was not repeated for the next album. Du kennst die Liebe nicht was re-recorded as the fifth and last single, with different vocals and a different instrumental backing. In 2002, Kerner recorded a bilingual version of Anyplace, Anywhere, Anytime with Kim Wilde.
werk/nena-feuer-und-flamme.listen: Listen to Feuer und Flamme and notice how Nena's voice carries the song, in the original German version.

werk/neu-neu-75.text:
This third album by the German krautrock duo came about after a break of several years, during which Michael Rother worked with Cluster in Harmonia. The musical wishes of Rother and Klaus Dinger had grown apart: Rother loved ambient, Dinger wanted a rougher rock sound. They resolved it by taking one side of the record each. The recording ran from December 1974 to January 1975 in Conny Plank's studio.

The first side, Rother's work, was recorded as a duo and sounds calm and floating. On the second side Dinger plays guitar and sings, while Thomas Dinger and Hans Lampe drum together. Hero is regarded as an example of protopunk and inspired John Lydon of the Sex Pistols, among others. David Bowie referred to it with the title of his album Heroes. In 1979 the NME reviewer Andy Gill gave the record the highest score.
werk/neu-neu-75.listen: Listen to Hero and notice the double drums and Dinger's raw vocals, which drive the pulsating rhythm section onward.

werk/new-order-brotherhood.text:
In 1986, New Order's fourth album was released on Factory Records. The group again sought the combination of post-punk and electronic music and divided the songs more or less over two sides: one with synthesizers, the other with guitars. Stephen Morris later called that a schizophrenic mood and thought it did not quite work. Peter Saville's sleeve shows a photograph of a sheet of titanium-zinc alloy, and early editions came in a metal sleeve.

Bizarre Love Triangle became the only single and the breakthrough in the United States and Australia. In All Day Long, influences of the Prelude from Richard Wagner's Das Rheingold can be heard. The ending of Every Little Counts sounds like a needle that keeps skipping. Critics later called it an underrated album, alongside its big single.
werk/new-order-brotherhood.listen: In Every Little Counts, listen to the odd ending, which sounds as if the needle of a record keeps getting stuck.

werk/new-order-get-ready.text:
Get Ready is New Order's seventh studio album. It was released in August 2001 on London Records and was the first in eight years, after Republic from 1993. Peter Hook said that the title could mean everything or nothing: the group was getting ready for the next phase in its musical life. The album is dedicated to Rob Gretton, the manager of Joy Division and New Order, who died in 1999. Billy Corgan sings along on one song and Bobby Gillespie on another.

The reviews were mostly positive. David Browne of Entertainment Weekly spoke of a stunning, self-assured return. Robert Christgau called it the group's best album in fifteen years. John Bush of AllMusic thought it was once again about songs and playing, rather than about pasted-on dance music. Not everyone was convinced: Mojo heard an old man getting out of a creaking armchair. Q put it among the fifty best albums of 2001.
werk/new-order-get-ready.listen: Listen to Crystal, the opener, and notice which instruments you hear. Does this sound more like rock or like dance to you?

werk/new-order-low-life.text:
Low-Life is New Order's third studio album and was released on 13 May 1985 on Factory Records. It is regarded as the moment when the group completed the transition from post-punk to dance rock. Synthesizers and samplers were given more room, but the rock elements of earlier work remained. Shortly before its release, the band filmed the concert film Pumped Full of Drugs in Tokyo with the new songs. Jonathan Demme directed the video for The Perfect Kiss.

The sleeve features photographs of the band members for the first time, taken with instant film. Designer Peter Saville was tired of conceptual sleeves. For the CD version, the buyer could choose which band member was visible through the sleeve. Critics praised the variety of soul pop, techno rock and quiet instrumental pieces. One reviewer called the album the point at which rock and electronics merged seamlessly.
werk/new-order-low-life.listen: Listen to The Perfect Kiss and notice how the electronic rhythms and the bass together drive the song forward.

werk/new-order-movement.text:
After the death of Ian Curtis in May 1980, the remaining members of Joy Division decided to carry on under the name New Order. Who should sing remained unclear for a long time; in the end Bernard Sumner took on that role. The arrival of Gillian Gilbert made a more electronic approach possible. The producer was Martin Hannett again, but relations had cooled. He left the group during the production of Everything's Gone Green, and it remained their last collaboration.

The album is a transition: gloomy post-punk with synthesizers, dub-like experiments and the beginnings of electropop. ICB refers to Curtis. The reception was lukewarm, but later the record received much praise as a bridge between Joy Division and the dance music that was still to come.
werk/new-order-movement.listen: In ICB, listen to the dark atmosphere of the song and remember that the title refers to Ian Curtis.

werk/new-order-power-corruption-en-lies.text:
Power, Corruption & Lies is New Order's second studio album and was released on 2 May 1983 on Factory Records. After the debut Movement from 1981, the group used far more synthesizers. The album combines their post-punk roots with electronic music. Kraftwerk and Giorgio Moroder are cited as influences. The single Blue Monday comes from the same sessions, but was released separately and was not on the album itself.

Dark songs such as We All Stand and Your Silent Face stand beside lighter pieces such as The Village. One critic called 5-8-6 a literal translation of early house. Peter Saville designed the sleeve with a painting of flowers by Henri Fantin-Latour and a colour code instead of the band's name. The record received much praise on release, and a Rolling Stone reviewer saw in it a declaration of independence from Joy Division.
werk/new-order-power-corruption-en-lies.listen: Listen to 5-8-6 and notice how the danceable electronic rhythms take the place of the post-punk guitars.

werk/new-order-republic.text:
Republic is New Order's sixth studio album and was released in May 1993. It was the first album after the end of their label Factory Records. According to bassist Peter Hook, the group had to make the record to save the Haçienda, the Manchester club in which they had money invested themselves. The atmosphere was bad: Hook and Bernard Sumner could barely stand each other. While Sumner worked with Johnny Marr as Electronic, the others wrote an instrumental album, which at Sumner's request disappeared into a drawer.

Regret, the first single, was the group's last song in the British top five. The album topped the British chart and was nominated for the Mercury Music Prize. Peter Saville designed the sleeve, with stock photographs of California that have been heavily edited. After a performance at Reading in August 1993, the group fell silent. Only in 1998 did they come together again, and their next studio album followed eight years later.
werk/new-order-republic.listen: Listen to Regret and notice what the instruments do beneath the vocals. What do you hear if you follow only the bass?

werk/new-order-technique.text:
After years in dark London studios, New Order chose Ibiza at Peter Hook's urging. The band worked there for four months, captivated by Balearic club music, after which the album was finished at Real World Studios in Wiltshire. Bernard Sumner had been influenced by the acid scene and his visits to Shoom in London. The band wanted to keep using dance rhythms, while Hook actually preferred to remain a rock band.

Technique was released on 30 January 1989 on Factory Records and is dance rock with influences of Balearic beat and acid house. It became the first New Order album to reach number one in England. Fine Time reached number eleven, and Round & Round and Run were also singles. Hook did not think it was an Ibiza dance record, but above all a summer sound. Critics praised the honest lyrics and the cheerful tone. Later Spin called it their best album, as a meeting of punk rock and synth-pop. A lawsuit over the guitar passage in Run was settled out of court.
werk/new-order-technique.listen: Listen to Fine Time and notice whether, besides the band, you also hear the influence of acid house and dance rhythms.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-from-he.text:
After the break-up of the Birthday Party, Nick Cave began a new project with Mick Harvey. They were joined by Blixa Bargeld of Einstürzende Neubauten, Barry Adamson and Hugo Race. The group took the name Bad Seeds from the last Birthday Party EP. From Her to Eternity was released in May 1984 on Mute Records, produced by Flood and the band themselves. Most of it was recorded at Trident Studios in London.

The album kicks the listener in the face less than the Birthday Party did. Cave himself said that he wanted to make the lyrics more important and that Bargeld's atmospheric, sparing guitar playing gave him room. J.G. Thirlwell co-wrote Wings Off Flies. The critical response was positive: the NME called the album visionary, and Pitchfork placed it at number 63 of the best albums of the 1980s in 2018.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-from-he.listen: Listen to From Her to Eternity and notice the sparing guitar and the dramatic vocals. How much room do they leave each other?

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-kicking.text:
The third album by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds consists entirely of covers. Cave and the band tried out a list of songs, including by bands such as The Loved Ones and The Saints, which in the end did not make the album. The choice always had a different reason. Sleeping Annaleah was a tribute to Tom Jones, with other songs he felt they had never been performed properly, and The Carnival Is Over had haunted his youth. The title comes from the Bible, from Acts 26.

Drummer Thomas Wydler played for the first time, so that the line-up consisted of five men. Mick Harvey wrote the string arrangements, which a Berlin ensemble played. Cave later played the album down, but said that it helped the band to play different kinds of music successfully, which benefited later records. The review in Spin was scathing and spoke of a smug lump.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-kicking.listen: Listen to The Carnival Is Over, a song that Cave knew from his youth, and notice how he sings it and how the band accompanies him.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-let-lov.text:
This eighth studio album by the Australian band was released in April 1994 on Mute Records. Nick Cave sings and plays organ and piano, Blixa Bargeld and Mick Harvey play guitar, Martyn P. Casey bass, Conway Savage piano and Thomas Wydler drums. Guests can be heard on a few songs, including Rowland S. Howard and Warren Ellis, who plays violin on Ain't Gonna Rain Anymore and on the second part of Do You Love Me?.

Three songs were released as singles: Do You Love Me?, Loverman and Red Right Hand. The album closes with that second part of Do You Love Me?. Later artists covered the songs many times. Metallica recorded Loverman, Arctic Monkeys made a version of Red Right Hand and PJ Harvey sang it for the television series Peaky Blinders.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-let-lov.listen: Listen to Red Right Hand and notice the unusual sounds beneath the vocals: according to the personnel list, an oscillator, bells and timpani, among other things, can be heard here.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-murder-.text:
Murder Ballads is the ninth studio album by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, released in 1996 by Mute Records. The band had already written the first song, O'Malley's Bar, during the recording of Henry's Dream. It did not fit on any record, so Cave conceived a whole album as an environment in which such songs could exist. The recording ran towards the end of the sessions for Let Love In, and there was even brief talk of a film with John Hillcoat.

The album consists of new and traditional murder ballads, in a mixture of blues, country, lounge and jazz. Stagger Lee, based on a traditional song, has been turned into reggae. In Where the Wild Roses Grow, Cave sings a duet with Kylie Minogue, which became a hit. Death Is Not the End, an arrangement of a Bob Dylan song, closes with a verse for each guest, including PJ Harvey and Shane MacGowan. The critical response on release was glowing.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-murder-.listen: Listen to Death Is Not the End. Count how many different singers take over a verse of this Dylan song, and hear how grim or, on the contrary, how light the album ends as a result.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-push-th.text:
Push the Sky Away was recorded at La Fabrique, a studio in a nineteenth-century country house near Saint-Rémy-de-Provence in France, with producer Nick Launay. It is the first album without founder Mick Harvey, who left in 2009, and the first since 1986 with Barry Adamson. The band entered the studio when Nick Cave had only half-developed ideas. The lyrics came about over a year in a notebook, partly by searching the internet for odd facts and Wikipedia articles. Cave said that the songs show how the internet influences events, fashions and absurdities.

Cave called the album a ghost baby in the incubator, with Warren Ellis's loops as a small, trembling heart. That fits the subdued atmosphere. We Real Cool even names Wikipedia, and Jubilee Street was released as a single. Billboard spoke of the band's commercial breakthrough: the album was number one in Australia and six other countries.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-push-th.listen: Listen to We Real Cool and notice the loops that keep running beneath the song like a soft little heartbeat.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-skeleto.text:
Skeleton Tree followed Push the Sky Away and was recorded between late 2014 and early 2016 in Brighton, at La Frette near Paris and at Air Studios in London. Nick Cave, Warren Ellis and Nick Launay produced it. On 15 July 2015, towards the end of the sessions, Cave's fifteen-year-old son Arthur died after a fall. Most of the material had already been written by then, but Cave adjusted lyrics afterwards. By his own account he had lost faith in narrative songs, so the lyrics are partly improvised and almost never directly about the event.

The sound is bare and less polished, with synthesizers, drum machines and loops. Dissonances, drones and song structures without verse and chorus give the album an avant-garde character. At its release the documentary One More Time with Feeling by Andrew Dominik appeared, intended to explain the context without interviews. Both received wide praise. The opening lines of Jesus Alone were seen in hindsight as prophetic.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-skeleto.listen: Listen to Jesus Alone and notice the opening lines and the subdued, bare sound beneath them.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-the-fir.text:
The Firstborn Is Dead is the second album by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds. It was released on 3 June 1985 on Mute Records and was produced by the band and Flood. The recording took place at Hansa Studios in Berlin. Cave later said that the city gave them the freedom to do anything, whereas in London, as Australians, they were quickly reined in.

The title refers to Jesse Garon Presley, Elvis's stillborn twin brother. The album returns to the southern United States, with references to Elvis and bluesmen such as Blind Lemon Jefferson. Tupelo is loosely based on a song by John Lee Hooker and is about Elvis's birthplace, mixed with images of the apocalypse. Wanted Man is an arrangement of a song by Bob Dylan and Johnny Cash, with a lyric of Cave's own.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-the-fir.listen: Listen to Tupelo and notice the bluesy atmosphere and the imagery in the lyrics, from a birth to the end of time.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-wild-go.text:
Nick Cave began the songs on New Year's Day 2023 and recorded them with Warren Ellis at Soundtree in London and at Miraval Studios in France. The first sessions, with only piano and synthesizer, sounded too bare. So the whole band came in, for the first time since Skeleton Tree from 2016. Radiohead's bassist Colin Greenwood also played. The 2022 European tour had given the group renewed enjoyment and a chaotic energy. Drummer Thomas Wydler called it perhaps the first real rock record he had played on.

The album sounds full, vital and joyful, unlike its dark predecessors. The title came from three song titles: Conversion was too religious, Joy could be misunderstood, so it became Wild God. Critics and public responded positively. The album was nominated for two Grammys, including Best Alternative Music Album.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-wild-go.listen: In Frogs, listen to the simple guitar line. Guitarist George Vjestica played it in one take, inspired by Wichita Lineman by Glen Campbell.

werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-your-fu.text:
This fourth album by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds was released on 3 November 1986 on Mute Records, initially as a double EP. The singer was deep in a heroin addiction at the time, and you can hear that in the melancholy, despairing atmosphere. Producer Flood told of the first day of recording: Mick Harvey came with the inside of an old grand piano, just the strings on a metal frame. He tuned a few notes and plucked them with a plectrum. That is how The Carny came about, and it set the tone for the whole record.

According to Harvey, the album gave the band a template to carry on with: it was organised rather than messy and sounded like their own. The singer later called it his favourite album. In 1987 the group played The Carny in Wim Wenders's film Der Himmel über Berlin. The record topped the British independent albums chart.
werk/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds-your-fu.listen: Listen to The Carny and notice the peculiar little piano sound from which the song is built. It came from the strings of an old grand piano.

werk/nick-drake-bryter-layter.text:
Bryter Layter is Nick Drake's second studio album and was released on 5 March 1971 on Island Records. Like his debut Five Leaves Left, it contains no songs for just guitar and voice. Drake was accompanied by members of Fairport Convention, among others, and by John Cale of the Velvet Underground. According to arranger Robert Kirby, he wanted arrangements reminiscent of the Beach Boys' Pet Sounds. The album had been planned before November 1970, but was shelved because Drake was dissatisfied with the sleeve. On his next record, Pink Moon, he played entirely alone.

The first reviews were mostly positive and praised above all Kirby's arrangements. One critic found the ten songs rather too similar to one another. Later Mojo called the album the most polished of his work. Songs such as Fly and One of These Things First returned in films.
werk/nick-drake-bryter-layter.listen: Listen to At The Chime Of A City Clock and notice how Robert Kirby's arrangements surround the guitar and the voice.

werk/nick-drake-five-leaves-left.text:
Five Leaves Left is Nick Drake's debut album. It was recorded between May 1968 and April 1969 at Sound Techniques in London and was released in 1969 on Island Records. Sound engineer John Wood later said that Drake recorded live, singing and playing alongside the string ensemble, without overdubs. The title refers to Rizla rolling papers, whose packets announced near the end that only five were left.

Richard Thompson of Fairport Convention and Danny Thompson of Pentangle, among others, played on the album. Robert Kirby, a friend from Cambridge, wrote the string arrangements for several songs, Harry Robinson for River Man. The sound is described as folk with a chamber music side: soft vocals, quiet guitar playing and wistful lyrics. The first reviews were mixed. Drake sold few records during his lifetime, but at the end of the 1980s more attention came, and later the album often appeared on lists of the best records of all time.
werk/nick-drake-five-leaves-left.listen: Listen to River Man and notice the strings around his voice and guitar. Try to hear how those arrangements give the song its own atmosphere.

werk/nick-lowe-jesus-of-cool.text:
In March 1978, Nick Lowe's solo debut, produced by himself, was released in England on Radar Records. The musicians were not credited on the sleeve, but Dave Edmunds and Billy Bremner, among others, played guitar. In the United States, Columbia compiled the album differently and gave it the title Pure Pop for Now People, a slogan that was already on the British sleeve.

Many songs are about the greed and superficiality of the music industry, such as Music for Money, Shake and Pop and Rollers Show, a parody of the teenage audience of the Bay City Rollers. Musically the album is refined and varied, but it shares the energy and the cynical tone of new wave. The critic Robert Christgau admired how the hooks come from sources such as the Beach Boys and the Boomtown Rats. The album was highly valued by the press.
werk/nick-lowe-jesus-of-cool.listen: Listen to Marie Provost and notice the sober, carefully chosen instrumentation and the restrained vocals. One reviewer called this the best-crafted lyric Lowe had written up to that point.
